findings.issue: Move records are fetched in bulk and zipped by index into `recordByName` with no null handling; unlike the version-group fetch at line 67, a 404/null record isn't filtered, so line 114 dereferences it and crashes the whole Pokémon page with a 500.
findings.suggestion: Filter nulls or null-guard the row build (skip the row / fall back to the raw name), mirroring the `.filter(Boolean)` already used at line 67.

findings.issue: The module mixes server-only concerns (process.env, an in-memory fetch cache on globalThis) with `apiUrl`, which is consumed by the shared `PokemonCard` component (app/components/PokemonCard.jsx:3,17). Importing PokemonCard into any client tree would silently produce relative/broken media URLs because `API_BASE_URL` is undefined in the browser.
findings.suggestion: Add `import 'server-only'` to lib/api.js and move `apiUrl`/the media-URL construction into a pure, client-safe helper module.

findings.issue: Uncapped fan-out: one request per learnable move of the selected game (hundreds in parallel on a cold cache) plus all version-group records at line 63. Fine against the bundled local API, but it would hammer a real remote service and has no concurrency limit.
findings.suggestion: Chunk the Promise.all (e.g. batches of 25-50) or use a small concurrency limiter; the process cache still makes it a one-time cost.

findings.issue: A non-404 API failure throws inside a server component with no `error.jsx` anywhere, so users get the framework's default crash page instead of a graceful one.
findings.suggestion: Add an `app/error.jsx` boundary (and consider `loading.jsx` for the heavy moves section).

findings.issue: Builds query state from `window.location.search` instead of next/navigation's `useSearchParams`, and needs an eslint-disable (line 43) to do it.
findings.suggestion: Use `useSearchParams()`; pages are force-dynamic so the Suspense-boundary caveat doesn't apply.

findings.issue: A move with no damage class renders an empty `<dd>` instead of the spec's em dash (same pattern at app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.jsx:118).
Descending sort reverses the already-tie-broken array, so rows tied on the sort key come out in the opposite order from ascending sort.
findings.suggestion: Sort with a direction-aware comparator (keeping missing-last) instead of reversing.

findings.issue: Plain `` bypasses next/image (and triggers the `no-img-element` lint); avoiding the optimizer config for a remote API is defensible but undocumented.
findings.suggestion: Either configure `images.remotePatterns` for API_BASE_URL and use next/image, or add a comment explaining the deliberate choice.

findings.issue: The process-lifetime cache is unbounded and never evicts; sanctioned by the spec today, but it will grow with every distinct resource touched.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is for a fixed 1,025-species snapshot; note the trade-off in the header comment or add a simple size cap.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Next 16 App Router implementation — async request APIs, notFound, generateMetadata, memoized server data layer, and exactly two well-behaved client islands — that I'd merge after one light round. The blocking asks are small: a null guard in the move-record assembly that would otherwise 500 a valid page, and hardening the server/client boundary around lib/api.js's `apiUrl`. Everything else (uncapped first-load fan-out, missing error boundary, a couple of display edge cases) is nits the team can pick up opportunistically.
